decks.domain: Traffic Signs, Warning and Guide Signs, and Construction Devices

cards.front: What do traffic signs tell you, and how do they carry meaning?
cards.back: Traffic signs tell you what actions you must take, warn you of possible hazards, and identify routes and locations, and their meaning is carried by color and shape as well as by words, letters, numbers and silhouettes.
cards.memory_hook: Act, warn, locate; color and shape

cards.front: What does the color red on a sign mean?
cards.back: The color red on a sign means an action is prohibited, and red appears on signs of various shapes.

cards.front: What do yellow and orange signs mean, and what shapes do they use?
cards.back: Yellow on a sign warns of hazardous or dangerous conditions and almost always appears on a diamond-shaped sign, while orange warns of road work and appears on rectangular or diamond-shaped signs.

cards.front: What do black and white signs mean, and which colors mark guide signs?
cards.back: Black and white signs indicate a required action and are always rectangular, while green, blue and brown are used on guide and information signs, mostly rectangular as well.
cards.memory_hook: Black-white commands, green blue brown guide

cards.front: How does yellow differ from orange on signs?
cards.back: Yellow warns of hazards on a diamond, while orange warns of road work on a diamond or rectangle.

cards.front: How do black and white signs differ from red signs?
cards.back: Black and white signs command an action and are always rectangular, while red signs prohibit an action and come in various shapes.

decks.domain: Traffic Signs, Warning and Guide Signs, and Construction Devices

cards.front: What is a stop sign, and what must you do at one?
cards.back: A stop sign is an eight-sided white-on-red sign meaning other traffic has the right of way, so you must always come to a complete stop and yield to approaching traffic before proceeding.

cards.front: Where do you stop at a stop sign, and what if you cannot see traffic?
cards.back: At a stop sign you stop at the stop line, or before the marked or unmarked crosswalk if there is no stop line, and if you cannot see traffic from that first stop you move ahead slowly and stop again where you can see approaching traffic.
cards.memory_hook: Line or crosswalk, creep, stop again

cards.front: What is a yield sign, and when must you stop at one?
cards.back: A yield sign is a triangular red and white sign meaning other traffic has the right of way, so be ready to stop, but you need to stop only when other traffic actually holds the right of way.

cards.front: How does a stop sign differ from a yield sign?
cards.back: A stop sign always demands a complete stop, while a yield sign demands a stop only when other traffic holds the right of way.

cards.front: At a stop sign without a stop line, where do you stop, and when twice?
cards.back: At a stop sign without a stop line you stop before the crosswalk, and when the view is blocked you creep forward and stop a second time where you can see traffic.

decks.domain: Traffic Signs, Warning and Guide Signs, and Construction Devices

cards.front: What do do not pass signs mark?
cards.back: Do not pass signs are rectangular signs marking places on two- or three-lane roads where you must not pass another vehicle.

cards.front: What is a no passing zone sign, and where is it placed?
cards.back: A no passing zone sign is a pennant-shaped yellow and black sign that supplements the do not pass sign, and it stands on the left side of the road pointing to the start of the no-passing zone.
cards.memory_hook: Yellow pennant, left side, zone start

cards.front: What does a pass with care sign mark?
cards.back: A pass with care sign is a rectangular black and white sign marking the end of a no-passing zone.

cards.front: How does a do not pass sign differ from the pennant?
cards.back: A do not pass sign is a rectangle marking the no-passing stretch itself, while the no passing zone pennant on the left merely points to where that stretch begins.

cards.front: How does a pass with care sign differ from a do not pass sign?
cards.back: A pass with care sign ends a no-passing zone, while a do not pass sign begins one.

decks.domain: Traffic Signs, Warning and Guide Signs, and Construction Devices

cards.front: What do speed limit signs show, and what must you obey?
cards.back: Speed limit signs are rectangular black and white signs that show the established maximum and minimum limits, which may apply only at certain times, under certain conditions or to certain kinds of vehicles, and you must drive neither faster than the maximum nor slower than the minimum.

cards.front: What does a reduced speed ahead sign tell you?
cards.back: A reduced speed ahead sign has the same color and shape as a speed limit sign and gives advance notice to begin slowing, and the new lower limit takes effect at the next speed limit sign.
cards.memory_hook: Start slowing, limit at next sign

cards.front: What do lane use control signs require?
cards.back: Lane use control signs are rectangular black and white signs showing that turns are required or unusual turns are permitted from specific lanes at an intersection, and you must move only in the direction shown for your lane.

cards.front: What do other alignment signs show?
cards.back: Other alignment signs are rectangular black and white signs showing where you must drive so traffic moves safely and smoothly.

cards.front: What do exclusion signs look like, and what do they do?
cards.back: Exclusion signs are rectangular and show either a red circle on white or a red circle with a red diagonal slash on black and white, and they restrict or prohibit vehicles, vehicle movements or other activities.

cards.front: What do the other regulatory signs look like and restrict?
cards.back: The many other regulatory signs are all rectangular with black or red lettering on a white background, and they restrict people, vehicles, weights, vehicle types, parking and similar matters.
cards.memory_hook: White rectangle, black or red words

cards.front: How does a reduced speed ahead sign differ from the speed limit sign?
cards.back: A reduced speed ahead sign only tells you to start slowing, while the speed limit sign after it is where the lower limit actually takes effect.

cards.front: How does an exclusion sign differ from worded regulatory signs?
cards.back: An exclusion sign uses a red circle, with or without a diagonal slash, to prohibit a movement or activity, while other regulatory signs use black or red lettering on white to state restrictions in words.

decks.domain: Traffic Signs, Warning and Guide Signs, and Construction Devices

cards.front: What do warning signs alert you to?
cards.back: Warning signs alert you to dangers that exist or may exist on or near the road, so be prepared to take safe and proper action when you see one.

cards.front: What do most warning signs look like, and which examples are pictured?
cards.back: Most warning signs are yellow diamonds carrying a black border and black symbols or words, and the examples pictured include divided highway, divided highway ends, hill, slippery when wet, pedestrian crossing, and lane ends or road narrows.

cards.front: What can the school sign mean, and what other warning sign is shown?
cards.back: One warning sign can mean either school crossing or school zone, and another warns of a traffic signal ahead.
cards.memory_hook: School crossing or zone, signal ahead

decks.module: Work zone devices and barricade stripes
decks.domain: Traffic Signs, Warning and Guide Signs, and Construction Devices

cards.front: Why are devices used in work zones, and what is their basic color?
cards.back: Construction and maintenance work areas use traffic control devices to guide drivers and pedestrians safely through the work zone and to protect highway workers, and orange is the basic color of these devices.

cards.front: What are the most common work zone devices?
cards.back: The most common work zone devices are signs, barricades, drums, cones, tubes, flashing arrow panels and flagpersons.

cards.front: What shape are most construction and maintenance signs?
cards.back: Construction and maintenance signs notify drivers of unusual or potentially dangerous conditions in or near work areas, most are diamond-shaped and a few are rectangular.

cards.front: What are channelizing devices, and what do they carry at night?
cards.back: Barricades, vertical panels, drums, cones and tubes are the channelizing devices most often used to alert drivers to work zone hazards and guide them through, and at night they often carry flashing or steady burning lights.
cards.memory_hook: Barricades, drums, cones; lights at night

cards.front: What do the diagonal stripes on a barricade mean?
cards.back: The diagonal stripes on a barricade or vertical panel point the way traffic should pass, with stripes sloping down to the right meaning bear right and stripes sloping down to the left meaning bear left.
cards.memory_hook: Stripes slope the way to go

cards.front: What are flashing arrow panels used for?
cards.back: Large flashing or sequencing arrow panels are used in work zones day and night to guide drivers into certain lanes and to show that part of the road ahead is closed.

cards.front: What do flagpersons wear and use?
cards.back: Flagpersons stop, slow or guide traffic through work zones, wear orange vests, shirts or jackets, and direct traffic with red flags or stop and slow paddles.

cards.front: What do stripes sloping right versus left mean?
cards.back: Barricade stripes sloping downward to the right mean bear right, while stripes sloping downward to the left mean bear left.

cards.front: How does an arrow panel differ from a flagperson?
cards.back: A flashing arrow panel steers drivers into a lane or announces a closure, while a flagperson with a flag or paddle stops, slows or guides traffic in person.

decks.domain: Traffic Signs, Warning and Guide Signs, and Construction Devices

cards.front: What do guide and information signs cover?
cards.back: Guide and information signs cover everything about your location and the location of places and services, including route markers, location and distance signs, park and recreation signs, and service information signs.

cards.front: How do guide sign colors differ from warning sign colors?
cards.back: Guide and information signs in green, blue or brown locate places and services, while warning signs in yellow describe hazards.
cards.memory_hook: Green blue brown locate, yellow warns
